gallery.title: File:RA-5C RVAH-6 in flight 1970.jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Navy
gallery.credit: U.S. Navy photo from the USS Kitty Hawk 1970-71 cruise book [1]
gallery.description: A U.S. Navy North American RA-5C Vigilante (BuNo 156624) of heavy reconnaissance squadron RVAH-6 Fleurs in 1970/71. RVAH-6 was assigned to Attack Carrier Air Wing 11 (CVW-11) aboard the aircraft carrier USS Kitty Hawk (CVA-63) for a deployment to Vietnam from 6 November 1970 to 17 July 1971. The RA-5C 156624 is today preserved at the National Museum of Naval Aviation at Pensacola, Florida (USA).
categories: Reconnaissance Heavy Attack Squadron 6 (United States Navy)

gallery.source: U-2S and F-5F VFC-111 at NAS Key West 2008
gallery.description: A U.S. Air Force Lockheed U-2S aircraft lands at Naval Air Station Key West, Florida (USA), on 1 May 2008, on the 48th anniversary of the downing of a U-2 flown by retired U.S. Air Force Capt. Gary Powers over the Soviet Union. Visible in the foreground is a U.S. Navy Northrop F-5F Tiger II (USAF s/n 84-0456) from composite fighter squadron VFC-111 Sundowners, an adversary squadron based at NAS Key West.

gallery.title: File:330-PS-2934 (USN 443986) (17595401352).jpg
gallery.artist: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
gallery.description: 330-PS-2934 (USN 443986):   Sub Rescues Disabled Airship.   A disabled airship nears the reach of Boca Chica Naval Air Station in two by an air-sea rescue boat which took over from USS Sea Poacher (SS 406).  The ZX-11 blimp while making a dummy attack of the submarine came in on a low attack and its propellers struck the surface of the ocean rendering it powerless.  The Sea Poacher attached a cable to the blimp’s mooring line and towed it to the beach.  At daybreak, sailors hauled the blimp ashore to a mooring mast.  Photograph released July 11, 1952.  (5/12/2015).

gallery.title: File:170907-N-QE668-002 (37131140825).jpg
gallery.artist: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
gallery.description:
170907-N-QE668-002 

KEY WEST, Fla. (Sept. 7, 2017) The Fleet Logistic Center supply warehouse at Naval Air Station Key West is used as a staging area for government vehicles from Naval Air Station Key West's Boca Chica Field. The warehouse is one of the highest points on the air station at 11 ft. above sea level. Non-essential active duty military, DOD civilians and their families have evacuated the base. Hurricane Irma is a Category 5 hurricane with sustained winds of more than 180 mph and is moving west-northwest at 17 mph. The storm is expected to impact the southeastern United States. (U.S. Navy photo by Lt. Joshua Andrews/Released)

gallery.title: File:170913-N-YL073-0013 (37269064705).jpg
gallery.artist: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
gallery.description:
170913-N-YL073-0013

KEY WEST, Fla. (Sept. 13, 2017) Sailors assigned to USS New York (LPD 21), clear debris at the Port Operations pier onboard Naval Air Station Key West, Fla., during humanitarian relief efforts following Hurricane Irma's landfall in Key West. The Department of Defense is supporting Federal Emergency Management Agency, the lead federal agency, in helping those affixed by Hurricane Irma to minimize suffering and as one component of the overall whole-of-government response efforts. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Shamira Purifoy/Released)
